root_cause.text: The Bluetooth MGMT `mesh_send()` handler in `net/bluetooth/mgmt.c` validated only the overall command length range and failed to verify that the flexible `mgmt_cp_mesh_send::adv_data[]` payload size exactly matched the embedded `adv_data_len` field, allowing truncated requests to be accepted and later read past the queued command buffer in the async mesh send path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `u16 expected_len;`, explicitly rejects `!send->adv_data_len || send->adv_data_len > 31`, and then checks `expected_len = struct_size(send, adv_data, send->adv_data_len); if (expected_len != len) return ... MGMT_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMS;` because previously the code only checked `len <= MGMT_MESH_SEND_SIZE || len > (MGMT_MESH_SEND_SIZE + 31)` and did not tie `len` to `adv_data_len`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an `expected_len` variable in `mesh_send()` to support mesh message length handling.
intent_record.what: A new local variable `u16 expected_len;` was added to `mesh_send()` alongside the existing local declarations.
intent_record.how: By introducing `expected_len`, the function can track or validate the length expected for mesh-send processing, likely supporting later size checking or message parsing logic at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten mesh send parameter validation by checking LE support, validating advertising data length, and rejecting malformed request sizes with the correct status.
intent_record.what: The function `mesh_send()` was changed to split one combined validation into multiple checks: it now returns `MGMT_STATUS_REJECTED` immediately if LE is not enabled, separately validates `send->adv_data_len` to ensure it is nonzero and no more than 31, computes `expected_len = struct_size(send, adv_data, send->adv_data_len)`, and returns `MGMT_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMS` if `expected_len` does not match `len`. The previous single condition that rejected when `!HCI_LE_ENABLED`, `len <= MGMT_MESH_SEND_SIZE`, or `len > MGMT_MESH_SEND_SIZE + 31` was removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the command handling now distinguishes between unsupported LE state, invalid advertised data length, and malformed payload size. This makes mesh send request validation stricter and more precise, preventing acceptance of packets whose buffer length does not exactly match the embedded `adv_data_len` field and improving the error status reported to callers.

This upper-bound check still only constrains total request length and does not validate the flexible adv_data[] payload against adv_data_len, leaving the async path vulnerable to reading past the queued buffer.
